summary: Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD in 2008 at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Fudan University, earning a BA by 2010, and completed a Magister Artium at the University of Munich.

Tara Doyle is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. At Emory University, she served as a lecturer in religious studies and director of the Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003), and was later Professor Emerita (attested 2026).
Tarapada Chowdhury (1907–1964) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Having succeeded Edward Hamilton Johnston by 1950, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Patna College (attested 1950).

Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a curator at the Royal Danish Library from circa 1962 to 1999 and at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1968 to 1999.

Taranatha Tarkavachaspati (1812–1885) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University (~1845–1872) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Tarthang Tulku (born 1935) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Tarthang Monastery and under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, later holding posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and the Nyingma Institute (~1972).

Tashi Densapa (born 1918) is a Tibetology and history scholar. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1978, 2002) and as director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 2008).

Tashi Rabgey is a scholar of Tibetology. Educated at University College Toronto, Cambridge, Magdalen College, and Harvard (~1998–2004), she has held posts at the University of Virginia (~2007–2011) and Georgetown University.

Tashi Samphel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tashi Tsering (born 1960) works in Tibetology, history, and linguistics. He served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1980–1992), became director of the Amnye Machen Institute (~1992), and was a professor at CIHTS (attested 2014–2019).

Tatiana Oranskaia (born 1950) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, later teaching at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996; 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato (1924–2021) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned his doctorate from Komazawa University (~1952–1978). He held faculty posts at Komazawa University from circa 1962 to 1995, as well as at Ryukoku and Tokai universities.

Tatsuo Hayashi (1896–1984) studied at Kyoto University (~1918–1921) and worked in philosophy. He held posts at Toyo University (~1925–1932), Hosei University (~1926–1930), Tsuda University (~1932–1944), Meiji University (~1946–1950), and Rikkyo University.

Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012), a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist, studied at Kyoto University (doctorate, 1962). He served on Kyoto University's faculty from 1956 to 1992, including as professor and dean, and later at the National Center for Science Information Systems.

Tavivat Puntarigvivat (born 1950) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and held posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and the World Buddhist University (attested 2013).

Taw Sein Ko (1864–1930) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed studies at the University of Rangoon, the Inns of Court (~1892–1893), and the Inner Temple (~1892–1893).

Teizo Iyanaga (1915–1983) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1938), he held academic posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo (~1949–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).

Tej Ram Sharma (born 1941) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (attested 1978).
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Lobsang Gyatso, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.
